I've saved the answers to `answer.json`. All eight are calculated, with one judgement call on question a that you should know about.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | `smb`, 336,941,863 |
| b. Customers with a paid order in Q3 | 247 |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | `acc`, 287,369,465 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refund total | u222@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders in Q3 | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 689,361 |
| h. Net sales growth, September vs August | -13.7% |

- **Segment rule for question a:** 25 email addresses are shared by accounts in different segments (for example, u11@ex.com is both smb and enterprise). Your rules don't say which segment such a person belongs to. I used the segment of the account that placed each order. The person-level grouping by email applies only to the customer counts and the refund ranking (b, e, f). smb is ahead by a wide margin (about 67 million), so assigning these people differently is unlikely to change the winning segment.
- **Data checks:** Order times all use one format and were shifted by +9 hours to KST before grouping by date, month and quarter. Segment values include ones like " consumer" and "Enterprise ", so I trimmed spaces and lowercased them. Every refund matches an order line, and no line is refunded more than once.
- **Range for d:** The data runs from May to October 2025, so "all time" here means those six months.

STATUS: DONE
